shipped_rows.title_o: Internet Users' Information Privacy Concerns (IUIPC): The Construct, the Scale, and a Causal Model

blind_target.title: Examining the influence of demographic factors on internet users’ information privacy concerns.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Our replication of the analysis by Zukowski and Brown (2007), regarding covariate effects, only confirmed the effects of gender on the privacy concerns in Japan.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Even though the correlation of IUIPC with age is significant, we consider it negligible in magnitude (0.113). Zukowski and Brown again obtain a different result from what we observed in Japan by accepting their hypothesis of an effect of age. Similarly, our correlation of IUIPC with the education and personal income levels yields negligible values of 0.03, and -0.05 respectively. Zukowski and Brown, however, do identify an effect of education, but also reject the effect of income.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly call the covariate analysis a replication. Age and education differ, while absence of income effect agrees; gender also differs. Earlier IUIPC replications cited solely for context are not targets.

luna_triage.reason: The Results/Discussion explicitly labels the covariate analysis as a replication of Zukowski and Brown's (2007) work. It retests their demographic effects on IUIPC in Japanese respondents; comparison shows some effect agreements and disagreements. The identity is directly cited and appears in References. The only supplied shipped original is Malhotra et al. (2004), a distinct paper; no supplied row represents Zukowski and Brown.
luna_triage.omission_quote: Our replication of the analysis by Zukowski and Brown (2007), regarding covariate effects, only confirmed the effects of gender on the privacy concerns in Japan.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Zukowski, T., & Brown, I. (2007). Examining the influence of demographic factors on internet users’ information privacy concerns.
luna_triage.duplicate_quote: The main aim of the present study was to verify the applicability of the IUIPC model of Malhotra et al. (2004) in Japan, especially focusing on the comparison to the original USA sample as well as on changes due to differences in time when conducting the studies (difference of eleven years).
